transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm just having some trouble sitting through things lately. Like at work, during sprint planning... or even on important calls, like for my mortgage. 

I just... I keep getting up. Even when I know I should stay put, I'll suddenly decide I need water, or I just have to go check something in the other room. So... yeah. I figured I should probably come in.
When did you first notice this trouble sitting still? Has this always been something you've struggled with, or is this more recent?

Um... I guess it's been a while. Since I was a kid, really. 

I don't know, I just remember... in elementary school, the teachers were always moving my desk. They had to keep telling me to sit down because I'd just pop up. And, you know, I'd talk before they called on me, or I'd just rush through my work, even if I knew how to do it. So... yeah. It's not really new.

Beyond just the difficulty sitting still and the interrupting in class, how much have these things actually gotten in the way of your life? Like, have they affected your grades, your jobs, or your relationships?

Um... I guess it causes some friction. Like, at work, and at home too. 

People just... they have to follow up with me a lot more than they used to. I don't know. I just worry that I'm becoming the unreliable one for planning tasks and things like that. Even though I'm really trying hard. So... yeah. It gets in the way a bit, I guess.

You mentioned rushing through your work even when you knew how to do it. These days, when you're trying to focus on something like reading an email or a document, do you find it hard to concentrate, or do you lose track of what you're reading?

Um... yeah, I guess. 

Like... if I start reviewing a pull request at work, or... I don't know, trying to read those mortgage documents. I start out fine, but... after a few minutes, I'll just realize I'm staring at the exact same section. And my mind is just... off somewhere else. Thinking about, like, five other things. So... yeah.

You mentioned these things have been going on since elementary school. But I want to clarify — were you actually struggling with focus and sitting still back then, or did those specific problems start more recently, like in high school or as an adult?

Um... yeah, I think I mentioned it earlier, but... it was definitely back then. Like, in elementary school. 

I just remember the teachers always having to move my desk around... or reminding me to stay in my seat because I kept popping up. And I'd talk before they called on me, or... just rush through everything, even if I understood the work. So... yeah. It definitely started back then, not in high school.

When you were in elementary school with all that desk-moving and getting called out for talking — were you having these same kinds of problems in other places too, like at home or playing with friends? Or was it mainly just at school?

Um... I don't really know. 

I guess... I mean, kids are just hyper, right? I don't really remember if it was an issue at home. I just remember the school stuff mostly. So... I'm not sure.

When you were playing with other kids or doing activities outside of school, like at home or with friends — did you notice yourself having trouble sitting still or focusing then, or was it really just the school environment where teachers were noticing these things?

I mean... I already said I don't really remember. 

It was a long time ago. I just remember the school part. I don't... I don't know about the rest of it. Kids just run around when they play, so... I don't know what to tell you.

When you were at home with your family — like during dinner or doing chores — did your parents or family members ever mention that you had trouble sitting still or paying attention, or was that mostly just something the teachers noticed at school?

Look, I... I really couldn't say. 

I mean, dinner was just dinner. We ate, we got up. I don't remember them making a big deal out of it. Like I said, it was mostly just the teachers who had a problem with it. I don't know what else you want me to say about it.

Think back to when you were maybe 8 or 9 years old — when you were doing things outside of school, like playing sports, video games, or hanging out with friends, did you notice yourself having trouble staying focused or sitting still then, or was it really just at school where that was happening?

I... I really don't know. It's the same answer. I just don't remember that far back. 

When you're playing outside or doing sports, you're running around anyway, so nobody cares if you aren't sitting still. I really just remember getting in trouble at school. That's... that's all I've got.

Let me ask it differently — when you were in elementary school, did your parents ever talk to you about being too energetic, or did they seem concerned about your behavior at home? Even if you don't remember exactly, do you recall them saying anything like that?

No. I... I don't think so. 

If they were concerned about it, they kept it to themselves. I just don't have any memory of them sitting me down to talk about my energy levels or anything like that. I feel like we're just going in circles here... I really don't have anything else I can tell you about it.

When you were in elementary school, did your parents or teachers ever say you were daydreaming a lot, or that you seemed distracted or forgetful about things you were supposed to do — like forgetting homework, chores, or instructions they gave you?

No, not really. I mean... I don't remember anyone saying I was daydreaming. 

I guess I might have forgotten a chore here or there, like any kid, but... no one made a big deal about me being distracted or forgetful. It wasn't like that.

You mentioned you don't remember much about home, but thinking about it now as an adult — when you look back, do you think the sitting-still and focus problems you're having now are new, or have they been there your whole life, even outside of school?

I don't think it's new. I guess... it's probably always been there. 

Like I said, I mostly just remember the school stuff. I do remember teachers moving my desk a lot... or having to remind me to stay in my seat. I guess I was always popping up. And I'd talk before I was called on, or just rush through all my work even when I understood it fine. So... yeah. It's not new.

When you were around 10 or 11 years old, outside of what happened at school, do you remember your parents ever having to tell you to slow down, or saying things like 'you're always on the go' or 'you never sit still'? Even if you don't remember the exact words, do you recall them saying anything like that?

No. I... I really don't remember anything like that. 

Like I said, my memory is mostly just the school stuff. If my parents were telling me to slow down at home, I just... I don't recall it. I really don't have much else to say about how things were at the house.

I know you don't remember a lot from back then, but let me ask you this — before you turned 12, when you were just hanging out at home or with friends doing regular stuff, did you ever get in trouble or have people complain that you were rushing through things, or that you weren't paying attention to what they were saying?

I don't... no. I really don't think so. 

Like I've been saying, I just don't remember much about being at home or with friends back then. If anyone was complaining about me not listening or... rushing, I don't have any memory of it. I just don't know.

I understand you mostly remember the school stuff. But let me ask you this more directly — before age 12, did you ever have trouble keeping your mind on things when you were doing something you actually enjoyed or wanted to do, like playing a favorite game or hobby?
No... I don't think so. If it was something I liked doing, I don't remember having an issue with it.

Before you turned 12, did anyone — like a parent, relative, coach, or scout leader — ever give you feedback that you were having trouble paying attention, sitting still, or staying organized in activities outside of school?

No, not really... not outside of school. Like I said, it was mostly just at school. I do remember some teachers in elementary school having to move my desk a few times. They were always telling me to sit down because I'd just... get up. Or I'd talk before they called on me. And they'd get frustrated because I'd rush through my assignments, even when I actually knew how to do the work. But outside of that... I don't really remember anyone else saying anything.

When you were in elementary school, did any of your relatives or family friends ever mention to your parents that you seemed restless, talked a lot, or had trouble sitting still when you were visiting or spending time with them?
No, I... I don't think so. I mean, I don't remember anyone saying anything like that to my parents. It was really just... just the school stuff.

I know you don't remember much from home, but thinking about it now — before you were 12 years old, do you think your parents would have said you had problems with attention, sitting still, or staying organized if someone had asked them directly?
I'm not really sure. Um... I don't think they would have. They never really made a big deal out of anything at home, so... probably not.
